- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 10% of 30d mean, model often misses the mean-reversion dip; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment is trending.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–2% to forecast to reflect stronger bearish momentum.
